records.source: וַיָּב֤וֹא אֵלַי֙ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים מִזִּקְנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ לְפָנָֽי׃פ
records.gloss: And came to me men of [the] elders of Israel and sat before me.
pieces: Some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat down in front of me.

L.1: And there came to me men from the elders of Israel, and they sat before me.

R.1: Some of the elders of Israel came and sat down with me.

decisions.choice: elders of Israel sitting before the prophet: leaders of the exiles come for a word from the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 8:1 and 20:1, the leaders of the exiles come to Ezekiel's house, apparently to ask the LORD something through him. What the LORD says in reply is about their hearts, not their question (14:3).

records.heading: Idols in the heart

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.2: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הֶעֱל֤וּ גִלּֽוּלֵיהֶם֙ עַל־לִבָּ֔ם וּמִכְשׁ֣וֹל עֲוֺנָ֔ם נָתְנ֖וּ נֹ֣כַח פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם הַאִדָּרֹ֥שׁ אִדָּרֵ֖שׁ לָהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: Son of man, the men these have brought up their idols upon their heart, and [the] stumbling block of their iniquity they have put before their faces; [should I] really let myself be inquired of by them?
pieces: Son of man, these men have taken idols into their hearts and placed before their faces the stumbling block that leads them into guilt. Should I let them consult {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} at all?

L.3: Son of man, these men have brought up their filthy idols into their heart, and the stumbling block of their iniquity they have set before their faces. Should I really let myself be consulted by them?

R.3: Son of man, these men have made idols the center of their lives. They have put right in front of themselves the very thing that makes them fall into sin. Why should I let them ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for anything?

decisions.choice: brought up their idols into their heart: they are devoted to idols in mind and will
decisions.reason: The idols may not be in their houses, but they are in their hearts. The heart is the center of thought and loyalty; these men come to the LORD's prophet while their loyalty lies elsewhere.

decisions.choice: the stumbling block of their iniquity: the idols, which make them fall into guilt
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in 7:19; 18:30 and 44:12. A stumbling block is something that trips a person up; they have set it right in their own path.

decisions.choice: "Should I really let myself be consulted?": the doubled verb expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question repeats the verb for emphasis. The LORD will answer, but not in the way they want (14:4, 7-8).

decisions.choice: filthy idols (L), idols (B, R); iniquity (L), guilt (B), sin (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these words in Ezekiel and the prophets.

records.source: לָכֵ֣ן דַּבֵּר־א֠וֹתָם וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִ֣ישׁ אִ֣ישׁ מִבֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ יַעֲלֶ֨ה אֶת־גִּלּוּלָ֜יו אֶל־לִבּ֗וֹ וּמִכְשׁ֤וֹל עֲוֺנוֹ֙ יָשִׂים֙ נֹ֣כַח פָּנָ֔יו וּבָ֖א אֶל־הַנָּבִ֑יא אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה נַעֲנֵ֧יתִי ל֦וֹ בָ֖א בְּרֹ֥ב גִּלּוּלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Therefore speak to them and say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Any man of [the] house of Israel who brings up his idols upon his heart, and [the] stumbling block of his iniquity puts before his face, and comes to the prophet, I Yahweh will let myself be brought to answer him in it, according to [the] multitude of his idols,
pieces: Therefore speak to them and tell them: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: When {{gender:anyone|any man}} of the house of Israel sets up idols in {{gender:their|his}} heart, puts the stumbling block of {{gender:their|his}} guilt before {{gender:their|his}} face, and then goes to the prophet, I {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will give {{gender:that person|him}} an answer, as the great number of {{gender:their|his}} idols deserves,

L.4: Therefore speak to them and say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: {{gender:Anyone|Any man}} of the house of Israel who brings up {{gender:their|his}} filthy idols into {{gender:their|his}} heart and sets the stumbling block of {{gender:their|his}} iniquity before {{gender:their|his}} face, and comes to the prophet, I {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will answer {{gender:them|him}} {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, according to the multitude of {{gender:their|his}} filthy idols,

R.4: So speak to them. Tell them this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Suppose people from Israel make idols the center of their lives and put right in front of themselves what makes them fall into sin. Then they come to a prophet. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will give them an answer {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, the answer their many idols deserve.

decisions.choice: I will answer him myself according to the multitude of his idols: the text as read
alternatives: "I will answer him by it", following the written consonants
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "by it"; the scribes' marginal reading has "he comes", giving "I will answer him as he comes with the multitude of his idols". The sense of both is that the LORD will answer such a person directly, and as his idols deserve, not with the oracle he wants.

decisions.choice: I the LORD will answer him myself: the answer is judgment, not an oracle
decisions.reason: The LORD will not give a word through the prophet to someone who clings to idols. He will answer in person, by acting against him (14:8).

decisions.choice: {{gender:anyone|any man}}; {{gender:their|his}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Any man" here means any person, as in the laws of Leviticus 17:3 and 20:2, which have the same form; the pronouns follow. Readable uses the plural "people", which needs no setting.

records.source: לְמַ֛עַן תְּפֹ֥שׂ אֶת־בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּלִבָּ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָזֹ֨רוּ֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י בְּגִלּֽוּלֵיהֶ֖ם כֻּלָּֽם׃ס
records.gloss: in order to seize [the] house of Israel by their heart, who are estranged from me through their idols, all of them.
pieces: so that I may lay hold of the hearts of the house of Israel, who have all turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to their idols.

L.5: in order to take hold of the house of Israel by their heart, since they have all become estranged from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} through their filthy idols.

R.5: I will do this to take hold of the hearts of the people of Israel. All of them have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to their idols.

decisions.choice: take hold of the house of Israel by their heart: to grip their hearts and bring them back
alternatives: to catch them out by what is in their hearts
decisions.reason: The verb means to seize or grasp. The LORD's direct answer is meant to lay hold of the people's hearts, which have gone over to idols, and turn them back (14:6). It may also mean that the LORD will expose them by what is in their hearts.

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר׀אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה שׁ֣וּבוּ וְהָשִׁ֔יבוּ מֵעַ֖ל גִּלּֽוּלֵיכֶ֑ם וּמֵעַ֥ל כָּל־תּוֹעֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם הָשִׁ֥יבוּ פְנֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Therefore say to [the] house of Israel, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Turn back, and turn away from your idols, and from all your abominations turn away your faces.
pieces: Therefore say to the house of Israel: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Repent! Turn away from your idols, and turn your faces away from all your detestable practices.

L.6: Therefore say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Turn back, and turn [yourselves] away from your filthy idols, and from all your abominations turn away your faces.

R.6: So tell the people of Israel that this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! Turn away from your idols. Stop doing all those disgusting things.

decisions.choice: turn back: repent, change direction
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn or return. Here it is the call to repentance that runs through Ezekiel (18:30-32; 33:11): to turn from idols back to the LORD.

decisions.choice: Come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the people are to turn back, as the context implies.

records.source: כִּי֩ אִ֨ישׁ אִ֜ישׁ מִבֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וּמֵהַגֵּר֮ אֲשֶׁר־יָג֣וּר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וְיִנָּזֵ֣ר מֵֽאַחֲרַ֗י וְיַ֤עַל גִּלּוּלָיו֙ אֶל־לִבּ֔וֹ וּמִכְשׁ֣וֹל עֲוֺנ֔וֹ יָשִׂ֖ים נֹ֣כַח פָּנָ֑יו וּבָ֤א אֶל־הַנָּבִיא֙ לִדְרָשׁ־ל֣וֹ בִ֔י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה נַֽעֲנֶה־לּ֖וֹ בִּֽי׃
records.gloss: For any man of [the] house of Israel, or of the sojourner who sojourns in Israel, who separates himself from after me, and brings up his idols upon his heart, and [the] stumbling block of his iniquity puts before his face, and comes to the prophet to inquire of him concerning me, I Yahweh will let myself be brought to answer him by myself.
pieces: For if {{gender:anyone|any man}} of the house of Israel, or of the outsiders who live in Israel, separates {{gender:themselves|himself}} from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, sets up idols in {{gender:their|his}} heart, puts the stumbling block of {{gender:their|his}} guilt before {{gender:their|his}} face, and then comes to a prophet to inquire of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} through him, I {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will answer {{gender:that person|him}} {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}.

L.7: For {{gender:anyone|any man}} of the house of Israel, or of the sojourners who sojourn in Israel, who separates {{gender:themselves|himself}} from following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and brings up {{gender:their|his}} filthy idols into {{gender:their|his}} heart and sets the stumbling block of {{gender:their|his}} iniquity before {{gender:their|his}} face, and comes to the prophet to inquire of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} through him, I {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will answer {{gender:them|him}} by {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}.

R.7: Suppose someone from Israel, or a stranger living in Israel, turns away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They make idols the center of their lives and put right in front of themselves what makes them fall into sin. Then they come to a prophet to ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for advice. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will answer them {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}.

decisions.choice: the sojourner who sojourns in Israel: the foreigner living among the people, under the same law
decisions.reason: Foreigners who settled in Israel were covered by many of the same laws, including those against idols and those of 14:8 (Leviticus 17:8, 10; 20:2). The wording of these verses follows the style of those laws.

decisions.choice: to inquire of me through him: to seek an oracle from the LORD through the prophet
decisions.reason: The person goes to the prophet to "inquire of the LORD", the usual phrase for asking God for guidance (1 Kings 22:5, 8). The LORD will not answer through the prophet but directly (14:4).

decisions.choice: {{gender:anyone|any man}}; {{gender:themselves|himself}}; {{gender:their|his}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: As in 14:4. "The prophet" keeps "him": the prophets in view are men.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֨י פָנַ֜י בָּאִ֣ישׁ הַה֗וּא וַהֲשִֽׂמֹתִ֨יהוּ֙ לְא֣וֹת וְלִמְשָׁלִ֔ים וְהִכְרַתִּ֖יו מִתּ֣וֹךְ עַמִּ֑י וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And I will set my face against the man that and make him a sign and bywords, and I will cut him off from [the] midst of my people; and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against that {{gender:person|man}} and make {{gender:them|him}} a sign and a byword. I will cut {{gender:them|him}} off from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.8: And I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against that {{gender:person|man}} and make {{gender:them|him}} a sign and a byword, and I will cut {{gender:them|him}} off from the midst of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: I will turn against that person. I will make them a warning to others, someone people talk about as an example. I will remove them from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I will set my face against him and cut him off: the words of the law against idolatry
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks as in Leviticus 17:10 and 20:3, 5-6, where he sets his face against the one who sins and cuts him off from his people. A "byword" is a name people use as a warning or insult (Deuteronomy 28:37).

decisions.choice: make him a sign: the verb form is unusual
alternatives: make him desolate, an object of horror
decisions.reason: The vowels of the verb point to a word meaning "make desolate" or "appall", but the letters fit "set" or "make". Either way the person becomes a public warning.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD (see 6:7)
decisions.reason: See 6:7.

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: As in 14:4. Readable says "that person ... them", which needs no setting.

records.source: וְהַנָּבִ֤יא כִֽי־יְפֻתֶּה֙ וְדִבֶּ֣ר דָּבָ֔ר אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ פִּתֵּ֔יתִי אֵ֖ת הַנָּבִ֣יא הַה֑וּא וְנָטִ֤יתִי אֶת־יָדִי֙ עָלָ֔יו וְהִ֨שְׁמַדְתִּ֔יו מִתּ֖וֹךְ עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And the prophet, if he is deceived and speaks a word, I Yahweh have deceived the prophet that, and I will stretch out my hand against him and destroy him from [the] midst of my people Israel.
pieces: And if the prophet is deceived and speaks a message, it is I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who have deceived that prophet. I will raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against him and wipe him out from among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

L.9: And the prophet, if he is enticed and speaks a word, I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have enticed that prophet; and I will stretch {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand out on him and destroy him out of the midst of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

R.9: If a prophet is fooled into giving such people a message, it is I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who have fooled that prophet. I will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power against him and destroy him from among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

decisions.choice: "I, the LORD, have deceived that prophet": the LORD gives a false prophet over to his own deception as judgment
alternatives: the LORD permits the deception but does not cause it
decisions.reason: The words are bold. The prophet who agrees to give an oracle to someone who clings to idols is himself caught in the lie he wanted to tell, and the LORD says that this too is his doing. The same thought appears in 1 Kings 22:19-23, where the LORD sends a lying spirit to the prophets of Ahab, and in 2 Thessalonians 2:11. The verse does not say that the LORD leads innocent people into sin: the deception falls on those who have already turned from him, and both are punished (14:10).

decisions.choice: deceived: enticed, persuaded into what is false
decisions.reason: The verb means to persuade or entice, often into something foolish (Jeremiah 20:7; 1 Kings 22:20-22).

decisions.choice: giving such people a message
decisions.reason: Readable says that the case is the one of 14:4 and 14:7: a prophet who answers people who cling to idols.

records.source: וְנָשְׂא֖וּ עֲוֺנָ֑ם כַּֽעֲוֺן֙ הַדֹּרֵ֔שׁ כַּעֲוֺ֥ן הַנָּבִ֖יא יִֽהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And they will bear their iniquity; like [the] iniquity of the inquirer, like [the] iniquity of the prophet it will be,
pieces: Both will bear their guilt; the guilt of the prophet will be the same as the guilt of the one who consulted him,

L.10: And they will bear their iniquity; as the iniquity of the inquirer, so the iniquity of the prophet will be,

R.10: Both the prophet and the person who came to him will be punished for their sin. The prophet's punishment will be the same as theirs.

decisions.choice: iniquity: guilt and its punishment
decisions.reason: To "bear iniquity" is to carry the consequences of one's guilt, as in the law (Leviticus 5:1; Numbers 14:34). The one who seeks a false word and the one who gives it are punished alike.

decisions.choice: will be punished for their sin
decisions.reason: Readable says what "bearing iniquity" means (m1).

records.source: לְ֠מַעַן לֹֽא־יִתְע֨וּ ע֤וֹד בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאַֽחֲרַ֔י וְלֹֽא־יִטַּמְּא֥וּ ע֖וֹד בְּכָל־פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֣י לְעָ֗ם וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: so that not they stray again, [the] house of Israel, from after me, and not they defile themselves again with all their transgressions; and they will be to me a people, and I will be to them God, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: so that the house of Israel will no longer stray from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or defile themselves with all their rebellions. They will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own people, and I will be their God, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.11: so that the house of Israel may no longer go astray from following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, nor defile themselves anymore with all their transgressions; but they will be to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a people, and I will be to them God, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.11: Then the people of Israel will not wander away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} anymore or make themselves unclean with all their sins. They will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: they will be my people and I will be their God: the covenant promise, as 11:20
decisions.reason: The aim of the judgment is not destruction but the restored covenant (see 11:20).

decisions.choice: transgressions (L); rebellions (B); sins (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this word: "transgression" at Literal, "crime" or "rebellion" at Balanced, "sin" at Readable.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.12: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

records.heading: Noah, Daniel and Job

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם אֶ֚רֶץ כִּ֤י תֶחֱטָא־לִי֙ לִמְעָל־מַ֔עַל וְנָטִ֤יתִי יָדִי֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ וְשָׁבַ֥רְתִּי לָ֖הּ מַטֵּה־לָ֑חֶם וְהִשְׁלַחְתִּי־בָ֣הּ רָעָ֔ב וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה אָדָ֥ם וּבְהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Son of man, a land, when it sins against me by acting faithlessly, and I stretch out my hand against it and break for it [the] staff of bread and send upon it famine and cut off from it man and beast,
pieces: Son of man, suppose a land sins against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by being unfaithful, and I stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against it, break its supply of bread, send famine on it and cut off from it both people and animals,

L.13: Son of man, a land, when it sins against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by acting faithlessly, and I stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against it and break its staff of bread and send famine upon it and cut off from it human and beast,

R.13: Son of man, suppose the people of a country sin against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by being unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. So I use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power against that country. I cut off its food supply and send a famine, and both people and animals die.

decisions.choice: a land, when it sins: a test case stated like a law
decisions.reason: The oracle sets out a general case in the style of the laws of Leviticus, then applies it to Jerusalem (14:21). The same pattern is repeated four times: famine (14:13-14), wild beasts (14:15-16), sword (14:17-18) and pestilence (14:19-20).

decisions.choice: acting faithlessly: breaking trust with God
decisions.reason: The word means a breach of faith, taking what belongs to God or betraying him (Leviticus 26:40; 2 Chronicles 36:14).

decisions.choice: break the staff of bread: cut off the food supply
decisions.reason: Bread was the "staff" that supported life. The expression comes from Leviticus 26:26 and is used in 4:16 and 5:16.

decisions.choice: supply of bread (B), food supply (R); people and animals (B, R)
alternatives: staff of bread; man and beast
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "staff of bread" and "human and beast". Balanced and Readable give the sense, as Leviticus 26:26 does at Readable.

records.source: וְ֠הָיוּ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ נֹ֖חַ דָּנִיֵּ֣אלוְאִיּ֑וֹב הֵ֤מָּה בְצִדְקָתָם֙ יְנַצְּל֣וּ נַפְשָׁ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: and were these three men in its midst, Noah, Daniel and Job, they by their righteousness would deliver their own lives, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: even if these three men, Noah, Daniel and Job, were living there, their righteousness would save only themselves, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: and [if] these three men were in its midst, Noah, Daniel and Job, they by their righteousness would deliver [only] their own lives, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: Even if Noah, Daniel and Job lived there, the right way they lived would save only themselves, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Daniel: perhaps Danel, a righteous man of ancient times, rather than the Daniel of the book of Daniel
alternatives: Daniel, the Jewish exile at the Babylonian court (Daniel 1-6)
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew spells the name Dan'el, without the letter found in the name of the book's Daniel; the scribes read it as Daniel. Noah and Job were righteous men of the distant past, and neither was an Israelite. Texts from ancient Ugarit, older than Ezekiel by many centuries, tell of Danel, a wise and just king who judged the cause of the widow and the orphan, and Ezekiel names a Danel again as a byword for wisdom in 28:3. Many think this ancient figure is meant. Others think of Daniel of the book of Daniel, a younger contemporary of Ezekiel in Babylon, known for his righteousness and wisdom. The name is written "Daniel", as the scribes read it.

decisions.choice: they would deliver only their own lives: righteousness cannot be passed on to others
decisions.reason: Noah's righteousness saved his family (Genesis 6:9; 7:1), and Job prayed for his sons and his friends (Job 1:5; 42:8). Here even such people would save no one but themselves; 14:16, 18 and 20 add that they could not save even their children. Chapter 18 makes each person answerable for their own life.

decisions.choice: their own lives: themselves
decisions.reason: The word often translated "soul" here means life, the living self.

decisions.choice: the right way they lived
decisions.reason: Readable says what "righteousness" means here: a life lived rightly before God.

records.source: לֽוּ־חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֛ה אַעֲבִ֥יר בָּאָ֖רֶץ וְשִׁכְּלָ֑תָּה וְהָיְתָ֤ה שְׁמָמָה֙ מִבְּלִ֣י עוֹבֵ֔ר מִפְּנֵ֖י הַחַיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: If wild beasts I cause to pass through the land, and they bereave it, and it becomes a desolation, with no one passing through because of the beasts,
pieces: Or if I sent wild animals through the land and they left it childless, so that it became a desolation that no one would pass through because of the animals,

L.15: If I made wild beasts pass through the land and they bereaved it [of children], and it became a desolation, with no one passing through because of the beasts,

R.15: Or suppose I sent wild animals through the country, and they killed the children. The land would become so empty and dangerous that no one would travel through it because of the animals.

decisions.choice: wild beasts that bereave the land: the curse of Leviticus 26:22
decisions.reason: In the covenant curses the LORD warns that he will send wild animals that "bereave you of your children" (Leviticus 26:22; compare 5:17).

records.source: שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵלֶּה֮ בְּתוֹכָהּ֒ חַי־אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אִם־בָּנִ֥ים וְאִם־בָּנ֖וֹת יַצִּ֑ילוּ הֵ֤מָּה לְבַדָּם֙ יִנָּצֵ֔לוּ וְהָאָ֖רֶץ תִּהְיֶ֥ה שְׁמָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: [were] these three men in its midst, [as] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, not sons and not daughters would they deliver; they alone would be delivered, and the land would be a desolation.
pieces: even if these three men were in it, as surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, they could not rescue sons or daughters. They alone would be rescued, and the land would become a desolation.

L.16: [even if] these three men [were] in its midst, [as] I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters; they alone would be delivered, but the land would be a desolation.

R.16: Even if those three men lived there, they could not save even their own children. As surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, only they would be saved, and the land would be ruined.

decisions.choice: as I live: the LORD's oath
decisions.reason: The LORD swears by his own life, the strongest oath possible (5:11; Numbers 14:21).

decisions.choice: their own children
decisions.reason: Readable says "their own children", which the comparison with Noah and Job implies (14:14 m2).

records.source: א֛וֹ חֶ֥רֶב אָבִ֖יא עַל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֑יא וְאָמַרְתִּ֗י חֶ֚רֶב תַּעֲבֹ֣ר בָּאָ֔רֶץ וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה אָדָ֥ם וּבְהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Or a sword [if] I bring upon the land that, and say, Sword, pass through the land, and I cut off from it man and beast,
pieces: Or if I brought a sword against that land and said, "Let the sword pass through the land," and cut off from it both people and animals,

L.17: Or [if] a sword I bring against that land, and I say, "Sword, pass through the land," and cut off from it human and beast,

R.17: Or suppose I bring war on that country. I say, "Let the sword go through the land," and both people and animals are killed.

decisions.choice: "Sword, pass through the land": war called up by the LORD's command
decisions.reason: The LORD commands the sword as if it were a person (compare 21:14-22). The sword stands for war and invasion.

records.source: וּשְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵלֶּה֮ בְּתוֹכָהּ֒ חַי־אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לֹ֥א יַצִּ֖ילוּ בָּנִ֣ים וּבָנ֑וֹת כִּ֛י הֵ֥ם לְבַדָּ֖ם יִנָּצֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: and these three men [were] in its midst, [as] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, not they would deliver sons or daughters, but they alone would be delivered.
pieces: even if these three men were in it, as surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, they could not rescue sons or daughters; they alone would be rescued.

L.18: and these three men [were] in its midst, [as] I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters, but they alone would be delivered.

R.18: Even if those three men lived there, they could not save even their own children. As surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, only they would be saved.

decisions.choice: the refrain of 14:16 repeated
decisions.reason: The words of 14:16 return with each of the four judgments.

records.source: א֛וֹ דֶּ֥בֶר אֲשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֑יא וְשָׁפַכְתִּ֨י חֲמָתִ֤י עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ בְּדָ֔ם לְהַכְרִ֥ית מִמֶּ֖נָּה אָדָ֥ם וּבְהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Or pestilence [if] I send into the land that and pour out my wrath upon it in blood, to cut off from it man and beast,
pieces: Or if I sent plague into that land and poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on it in bloodshed, to cut off from it both people and animals,

L.19: Or [if] pestilence I send into that land and pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on it with blood, to cut off from it human and beast,

R.19: Or suppose I send disease into that country and pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on it, and death takes both people and animals.

decisions.choice: in blood: in death
decisions.reason: "Blood" here means death, the loss of life the plague brings, as pestilence and blood are paired in 5:17 and 28:23.

decisions.choice: pestilence (L); plague (B); disease (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this word, from the Jeremiah table.

records.source: וְנֹ֨חַ דָּנִיֵּ֣אלוְאִיּוֹב֮ בְּתוֹכָהּ֒ חַי־אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אִם־בֵּ֥ן אִם־בַּ֖ת יַצִּ֑ילוּ הֵ֥מָּה בְצִדְקָתָ֖ם יַצִּ֥ילוּ נַפְשָֽׁם׃פ
records.gloss: and Noah, Daniel and Job [were] in its midst, [as] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, not son and not daughter would they deliver; they by their righteousness would deliver their own lives.
pieces: even if Noah, Daniel and Job were in it, as surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, they could save neither son nor daughter. They would save only themselves by their righteousness.

L.20: and Noah, Daniel and Job [were] in its midst, [as] I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, they would deliver neither son nor daughter; they by their righteousness would deliver [only] their own lives.

R.20: Even if Noah, Daniel and Job lived there, they could not save even a son or a daughter. As surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, the right way they lived would save only themselves.

decisions.choice: Noah, Daniel and Job: the three righteous men of 14:14
decisions.reason: See 14:14 for "Daniel".

records.source: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה אַ֣ף כִּֽי־אַרְבַּ֣עַת שְׁפָטַ֣י׀הָרָעִ֡ים חֶ֠רֶב וְרָעָ֞ב וְחַיָּ֤ה רָעָה֙ וָדֶ֔בֶר שִׁלַּ֖חְתִּי אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לְהַכְרִ֥ית מִמֶּ֖נָּה אָדָ֥ם וּבְהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: How much more when my four judgments, the evil, sword and famine and wild beasts and pestilence, I send against Jerusalem to cut off from it man and beast!
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: How much worse it will be when I send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} four terrible judgments against Jerusalem, sword, famine, wild animals and plague, to cut off from it both people and animals!

L.21: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: How much more when I send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} four evil judgments, sword and famine and wild beasts and pestilence, against Jerusalem, to cut off from it human and beast!

R.21: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: It will be even worse when I send all four of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} terrible punishments against Jerusalem, war, famine, wild animals and disease. People and animals there will die.

decisions.choice: four evil judgments: sword, famine, wild beasts and pestilence together, as in 5:17
decisions.reason: The four disasters of 14:13-20 now come on Jerusalem all at once, as threatened in 5:17 and in the curses of Leviticus 26:22-26. Revelation 6:8 names the same four.

decisions.choice: how much more: if one disaster would leave only the righteous alive, four together will be worse still
decisions.reason: The argument moves from the test cases to the real case of Jerusalem.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֨ה נֽוֹתְרָה־בָּ֜הּ פְּלֵטָ֗ה הַֽמּוּצָאִים֮ בָּנִ֣ים וּבָנוֹת֒ הִנָּם֙ יוֹצְאִ֣ים אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וּרְאִיתֶ֥ם אֶת־דַּרְכָּ֖ם וְאֶת־עֲלִֽילוֹתָ֑ם וְנִחַמְתֶּ֗ם עַל־הָֽרָעָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֵבֵ֨אתִי֙ עַל־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵבֵ֖אתִי עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And behold, will be left in it survivors who are brought out, sons and daughters; behold, they [are] coming out to you, and you will see their way and their deeds, and you will be comforted concerning the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, all that I have brought upon it.
pieces: Yet there will be survivors left in it, sons and daughters brought out of it. When they come out to you and you see their conduct and their actions, you will be consoled over the disaster I have brought on Jerusalem, over everything I have brought on it.

L.22: Yet look, there will be left in it survivors who are brought out, sons and daughters. Look, they are coming out to you, and you will see their way and their deeds, and you will be comforted about the evil that I have brought on Jerusalem, all that I have brought on it.

R.22: But some people will survive. Some sons and daughters will be brought out of the city. They will come to you in exile, and you will see how they live and what they do. Then you will be comforted about the disaster I brought on Jerusalem, about everything I did to it.

decisions.choice: the survivors will show by their conduct why the judgment came, and so comfort the exiles
alternatives: the survivors are a faithful remnant whose goodness comforts the exiles
decisions.reason: Contrary to the rule of 14:14-20, some sons and daughters will escape. They are not spared because they are righteous: their "way and deeds" (a phrase Ezekiel uses for wicked conduct, 20:43-44; 36:17-19) will show the exiles that the LORD was right to judge the city. The comfort is that of seeing that the disaster was not senseless (14:23).

decisions.choice: the evil: the disaster
decisions.reason: The word can mean moral evil or harm; here it is the calamity the LORD brought on Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: come to you in exile
decisions.reason: Readable says where the survivors come: to the exiles in Babylon.

records.source: וְנִחֲמ֣וּ אֶתְכֶ֔ם כִּֽי־תִרְא֥וּ אֶת־דַּרְכָּ֖ם וְאֶת־עֲלִֽילוֹתָ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֗ם כִּי֩ לֹ֨א חִנָּ֤ם עָשִׂ֨יתִי֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֣יתִי בָ֔הּ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And they will comfort you, when you see their way and their deeds, and you will know that not without cause I have done all that I have done in it, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: They will console you when you see their conduct and their actions, for you will know that I did not act without reason in all that I did there, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.23: And they will comfort you when you see their way and their deeds, and you will know that not without cause have I done all that I have done in it, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.23: When you see how they live, you will feel comforted, because you will know that I had a good reason for everything I did to Jerusalem, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: not without cause: the judgment was just
decisions.reason: The chapter ends where 14:22 pointed: the exiles will see that the LORD did nothing to Jerusalem without good reason.
